name: Monitoring
description: The adversary is monitoring the information he is providing to the world to take appropriate actions if required.

subtechniques.name: Intrusion Detection System (IDS)
subtechniques.description: An intrusion detection system is a device or software application that monitors a network or systems for malicious activity or policy violations. Any intrusion activity or violation is typically either reported to an administrator or collected centrally using a security information and event management system

subtechniques.name: Monitor account activity
subtechniques.description: Monitoring account activity is important to detect unauthorized access, such as failed logins, successful logins, changes to account, and so on.

subtechniques.name: Warrant canary
subtechniques.description: Allows users to figure out if they have been compromised by LEA orders.

procedures.name: Google alerts
procedures.description: Google Alerts are email updates of the latest relevant Google results (web, news, etc.) based on your queries. Cybercriminals might use Google Alerts to receive notifications about information about themselves (self-doxing). https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/4815696?hl=en

procedures.name: Haven
procedures.description:
Haven: keep Watch is an Android application that leverages on-device sensors to provide monitoring and protection of physical spaces. Haven turns any Android
phone into a motion, sound, vibration and light detector, watching for
unexpected guests and unwanted intruders. https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.havenapp.main&hl=en

procedures.name: MXtoolbox
procedures.description: Mxtoolbox’s blacklists can be leveraged to determine if certain emails or IP’s are listed on a blacklist. https://mxtoolbox.com/blacklists.aspx
